analysis: Examined the three changed regions. (1) TensorParallelCheck.swift header comment (lines 25-26) is documentation only. (2) TensorParallelCheck.swift lines 526-529 add a `gemma` subcommand that dispatches to GemmaCheck.run, next to the existing `glm` and `qwen-prefill` dispatches. It is a developer or qualification CLI that runs before Options parsing and before ProcessForcedExit, signal routing and the deadline are armed (lines 579-582). The GemmaCheck implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so its file I/O, deadline handling and any sealed or bench reduction path are unreviewed. This matches the existing glm and qwen-prefill pattern and is not a provider-runtime path. The tool's sealed-bench mode stays explicitly labelled BENCH-only (unauthenticated ephemeral key exchange, lines 308-318) and is unchanged by this PR. (3) CapabilityCommandCheck.swift line 185 is a test expectation change: Gemma 4 capability now expects supportedGenerationModes == [.pipeline, .tensorParallel]. The check only asserts what Gemma4ResidentCapabilityMetadata should advertise. The producer change, the coordinator's handling of the new tensorParallel mode for Gemma, and the TP reduction's trust/encryption of inter-rank traffic are outside the supplied units. Open integration questions: whether Gemma4ResidentCapabilityMetadata and the runtime enable tensorParallel for Gemma with the same peer authentication and sealed-reduction guarantees as the Qwen rows, and whether GemmaCheck.swift writes reports or reads files with safe bounds. No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied lines. Threat IDs such as TB-002, TB-007 and A-001 are the relevant ones for any further review of the Gemma TP runtime.
